correctness.rationale: For all y, pairwise divisor indicator products average to 1/lcm(d,e) over an exact common period. Expanding gcd(d,e) as a sum of totients proves the displayed exact quadratic form with harmonic-floor coefficients. The summatory totient estimate yields the logarithmic coefficient 6/pi² and convergence of the rescaled totient measure on compact positive t-intervals. The weighted logarithmic-width cancellation gives G(t)=O(t) near zero, establishing a uniform O(epsilon²) small-t tail; otherwise G(t)=v+O(t) gives variance (6/pi²)v²log y+O(1). The dyadic contrast is positive by G(t)=-1 on (2,4). The actual packaged rational-arithmetic checker exhaustively compares complete periods at y=1,2,3 and makes additional finite numerical checks; it is corroboration, not proof of the limit.

originality.rationale: The claim is a necessary-and-sufficient classification of all fixed proportional-window linear combinations by bounded variance and a precise harmonic-floor integral for balanced contrasts. Searches of prior indexed statements, direct source abstracts, and relevant primary HTML found frequency and tail questions rather than the claimed joint covariance and contrast limit. This is a qualified literature-led originality assessment, not a proof of historical uniqueness. Kovaleva’s incomplete conference synopsis poses a substantive unresolved implicit-overlap risk.

value.rationale: A natural covariance question for the dyadic-divisor count variable studied by Ford, Gabdullin and Pratt has a universal rank-one answer, but balanced combinations escape the divergent fluctuation direction and have a computable finite variance. The sharp iff cancellation hyperplane and positive adjacent-window limiting difference distinguish joint arithmetic dependence from separate divisor-presence frequencies. This gives a natural structural classification with an explicit constant, while not claiming distributional limit laws or downstream consequences.
